sentences.text: SRSJ 4.

Case of the petitioners, in brief, is that based upon the report said to have been lodged by one Vurukuti Srinivasa Rao, S/o Mahalakshmi, resident of Visakhapatnam, the 4th respondent registered Crime No.80 of 2023 of Dwaraka Town Police Station on 21.08.2023 for the offences under Section 420, 409, 120-B of IPC.

The crime was registered against the Manager/Foreman of Seethampet Branch of Margadarshi Chit Fund Private Limited (for brevity "MCFPL").
5.
Brief contents of complaint are that, defacto- complainant joined as subscriber of chit at petitioner branch for Rs.10,00,000/- for 50 months and he paid 20 months subscription.
Thereafter he stood as successful bidder and he submitted sureties, however, the prized amount was not released by showing various reasons.
The foreman also stated that since the defacto complainant stood as surety in another chit, the amount would be adjusted and the remaining amount will be paid after completion of chit.
After completion of chit, defacto complainant requested to pay the amount however it was dodged and finally cheque for Rs.18,609/- was handed over.
When the defacto-complainant enquired foreman, he inturn, replied that all the accounts would be SRSJ available with head office and the cheque sent by head office was handed over to complaint.
Foreman also threatened him.

On 17.08.2023 when the District Registrar called the complainant and asked about chit details, he complained about injustice caused to him and he came to know that Management caused him a loss of Rs.84,900/-.
Based on the said complaint, the above crime was registered.

6. The 4th respondent-Sub Inspector of Police issued notice dated 05.10.2023 under Section 102 of Cr.P.C to 6th respondent-Branch Manager of the 5th Respondent-Bank to freeze 3 accounts of MCFPL lying with 5th respondent-Bank of Dwaraka Nagar Branch, Viskhapatnam.
The 4th respondent served notice to Branch Manager on 05.10.2023.
On the same day, 6th respondent through letter dated 05.10.2023 intimated to 4th respondent that 3 accounts were totally freezed.
The bank also furnished copy to the petitioners regarding freezing of accounts.
Aggrieved by the same, the above writ petition is filed.

7. Sri Posani Venkateswarlu, learned senior counsel for petitioners would submit that Seethampet Branch/Foreman SRSJ of the petitioners is overseeing 126 chit groups within this branch and there are total 5795 subscribers.
As on the date of freezing of accounts, total balance in the respective accounts is Rs.7,69,76,486/-.
Learned senior counsel would submit that as per the Section 22 of the Chit Funds Act, 1982 (for short "the Act") two separate accounts shall be opened in the Bank.
Account No.1 is to deposit monthly installment payments of subscribers and Account No.2 is to deposit prize chit amount that remains unclaimed or unpaid for 30 days.
As per Section 30 of the Act, a separate account needs to be opened.
Thus, a total of 3 accounts were opened and they are being operated.

sentences.text: Learned senior counsel would submit that the complainant was highly irregular subscriber and he came a successful bidder on 22.02.2020 for a prize amount of Rs.8,65,000/- and thereafter he failed to pay the subscriptions from March, 2020 and did not draw the prize amount by submitting sufficient sureties.
He would also submit that due to freezing of accounts, the Foreman is unable to collect and deposit the monthly subscription amounts of 126 chit groups.

He would also submit that SRSJ under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. bank account of a person can be freezed only when the transactions in the bank account have direct nexus with the offence alleged against the accused.
He would also submit that in the facts of the case, writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable.

9. Sri Kasa Jagan Mohan Reddy, learned Special Government Pleader for respondents 1 to 4 would submit that writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is not maintainable and the petitioners have to approach the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 451 of Cr.P.C.

He would further submit that investigation is in progress and the 4th respondent issued notice under Section 102 of Cr.P.C. to freeze the accounts, strictly in accordance with law.
10.

The points for consideration in this interlocutory application are:
1) Whether the writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable?
2) Whether the petitioners made out prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss for grant interim order?
SRSJ 11.

In Godrej Sara Lee Ltd Vs. Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-Assessing Authority and Others1,
the Hon'ble Apex Court held thus:
"4. Before answering the questions, we feel the urge to say a few words on the exercise of writ powers conferred by Article 226 of the Constitution having come across certain orders passed by the high courts holding writ petitions as "not maintainable" merely because the alternative remedy provided by the relevant statutes has not been pursued by the parties desirous of invocation of the writ jurisdiction.

sentences.text: The power to issue prerogative writs under Article 226 is plenary in nature.
Any limitation on the exercise of such power must be traceable in the Constitution itself.
Profitable reference in this regard may be made to Article 329 and ordainments of other similarly worded articles in the Constitution.
Article 226 does not, in terms, impose any limitation or restraint on the exercise of power to issue writs.

While it is true that exercise of writ powers despite availability of a remedy under the very statute which has been invoked and has given rise to the action impugned in the writ petition ought not to be made in a routine manner, yet, the mere fact that the petitioner before the high court, in a given case, has not pursued the alternative remedy available to him/it cannot mechanically be construed as a The Branch Manager/Foreman vs The State Of Ap on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26178524/
3 ground for its dismissal.

sentences.text: It is axiomatic that the high courts (bearing in mind the facts of each particular case) have a discretion whether to entertain a writ petition or not.

One of the self-imposed restrictions on the exercise of power under Article 226 that has evolved through judicial precedents is that the high courts should normally not entertain a writ petition, where an effective and efficacious alternative remedy is available.

At the same time, it must be remembered that mere availability of an alternative remedy of appeal or revision, which the party invoking the jurisdiction of the high court under Article 2023 SCC OnLine SC 95 SRSJ 226 has not pursued,
would not oust the jurisdiction of the high court and render a writ petition "not maintainable".

In a long line of decisions, this Court has made it clear that availability of an alternative remedy does not operate as an absolute bar to the "maintainability"
of a writ petition and that the rule, which requires a party to pursue the alternative remedy provided by a statute, is a rule of policy, convenience and discretion rather than a rule of law.

Though elementary, it needs to be restated that "entertainability"
and "maintainability" of a writ petition are distinct concepts.
The fine but real distinction between the two ought not to be lost sight of.

The objection as to "maintainability" goes to the root of the matter and if such objection were found to be of substance, the courts would be rendered incapable of even receiving the lis for adjudication.
On the other hand, the question of "entertainability" is entirely within the realm of discretion of the high courts, writ remedy being discretionary.

A writ petition despite being maintainable may not be entertained by a high court for very many reasons or relief could even be refused to the petitioner, despite setting up a sound legal point, if grant of the claimed relief would not further public interest.

Hence, dismissal of a writ petition by a high court on the ground that the petitioner has not availed the alternative remedy without, however, examining whether an exceptional case has been made out for such entertainment would not be proper."

12. Thus, a perusal of the expression of the Hon'ble Apex Court makes it clear that mere availability of an alternative remedy is not a bar to maintain the writ petition, in a given case, if the petitioner satisfies the infringement of right.
In view of the same, this Court is of the opinion that writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India is maintainable.
SRSJ 13.
Case at hand, 2nd petitioner has been conducting chit business.

A perusal of the provisions of the Act makes it clear that jurisdictional Registrar is having over all control at the helm of affairs of Chit at every stage till the termination and even after termination till the disputes are resolved by way of arbitration.
Thus, jurisdictional Registrars, as per the provisions of the Act have been monitoring the affairs of every registered chit company.

Even before applying for sanction under Section 4 of the Act, the Foreman shall deposit in the name of Registrar an amount equal to 50% of gross chit amount in cash in appropriate bank and 50% in the form of guarantee from appropriate bank.

Thus,
the interest of each of the subscribers has been safe guarded.

sentences.text: A perusal of the complaint would disclose that the complainant stood as successful bidder in the chit and he submitted sureties, however the amount not released.
Finally cheque was issued for amount of Rs.18,609/-.
In the complaint it was alleged many infirmities on the part of foreman.
On 17.08.2023 when the District Registrar called the complainant and asked about chit details, he complained SRSJ about injustice and he came to know that Management caused him a loss of Rs.84,900/-.

The material papers filed along with writ petition Exhibits P5 and P6, prima facie show that defacto complainant joined as member of Chit Ref : LT 52X SP-28 for a value of Rs.10,00,000/-
with a monthly subscription of Rs.20,000/- for 50 months.
In case of any default on the part of foreman, Act itself, prescribes remedies.
Whether the complainant was properly paid the prized amount or not is a matter to be investigated into.
Indeed, the 4th respondent has been proceeding with investigation.
15. For the freezing of three accounts, referred to supra, as per Section 102 of Cr.P.C, there must be nexus with the offence alleged.

As seen from the averments in the writ affidavit there are total 5795 subscribers with 126 chit groups and defacto complainant is one of the members in one chit group for chit value of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The total amount freezed in 3 accounts referred to supra comes to Rs.7,69,76,486/-.
No complaint was made by any of the members of other chit groups.

Thus,
freezing of three bank accounts, in the opinion of this Court, will cause prejudice to subscribers of 126 chit groups.
Making allegations simplicitor SRSJ for the purpose of taking aid of Section 102 of Cr.P.C is not sufficient and proper.

It must be shown that allegation is found on such material so as to at least create reasonable suspension that the amount in the accounts is having some nexus or possibility of having nexus with the commission of offence.
After completion of investigation, the true facts will come to light.
However, freezing of 3 accounts, at this stage, will cause irreparable loss and hardship.
The loss caused to the petitioners will not be compensated for at a later point in time.
16. Registration of the Chit itself with Registrar, the petitioners made out prima facie case.
One of chit subscribers, among 5795 subscribers, after completion of chit period, made a complaint alleging irregularities.
In that connection freezing the three accounts of petitioners which involved the business transactions of others will cause irreparable loss which cannot be compensated at a later point in time.
Thus, this Court is of the opinion that balance of convenience is in favour of petitioners for grant of interim relief.

Thus, freezing of three accounts, referred to supra, needs to be suspended for the time being till a further SRSJ decision in the writ petition and the counter affidavit to be filed by the respondents.

Though, the learned Special Government Pleader would submit that the main relief and interim relief sought for in the writ petition are one and the same and hence interim relief cannot be granted at this stage, in the facts and circumstances of this case,
unless interim order is granted, it will cause irreparable loss to the petitioners.
17.
In view of discussion supra, the notice, under Section 102 Cr.P.C., issued by the 4th respondent to freeze three accounts, referred to supra, is suspended pending further orders.

The respondents 5 and 6 shall defreeze the accounts of the petitioners Margadarsi Chit Funds Private Limited,
Seethampet Branch vide Account Nos.010611100001884, 010611100001893 and 010611100001909 of Union Bank of India, Dwaraka Nagar Branch, Visakhapatnam forthwith.
However, this order will not come in the way of 4th respondent in proceeding with its investigation in connection with Crime No.80 of 2023 of Dwaraka Police Station, Visakhapatnam.
